prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Revise the supplied coastal cyberpunk roller coaster DESIGN REFERENCE. Its VISUAL STYLE is accepted by the user: lock the faceted stylized coastal island, clear modular industrial architecture, ivory/petrol/copper materials, cyan and restrained coral technical lighting, approachable helmeted explorer character scale, polished browser-game art instead of photorealism. User now wants the RIDE substantially larger, more thrilling and more complex, 1.5–2 times the previous facility scale. Create a new coherent DAYLIGHT master reference, roughly 1.8 times the LAND AREA of the source, conceptual footprint 110 by 130 meters, on an expanded connected grassy coastal headland. Widen the composition so the whole facility and entrance still fit. Keep the entrance plaza, six-lock gate, three distinct intent devices and covered station visibly foreground and recognizably the same design family. Make ONE continuous physically plausible roller coaster route for ONE train; maintain double rails and believable support beams and generous crossing clearances. The ride is now the protagonist, not a decorative edge of the plaza. Explicit ride silhouette: 1) an asymmetric 40–45 m mechanical lift tower well above everything, with visible service stairs/catwalk and a crest; 2) a prominent steep approximately 70-degree first drop diving into a low carved-rock trough; 3) a fast low-level track skimming through coastal rock cuts, safely landward of the sea; 4) two distinctly shaped airtime hills, one tall and one lower; 5) one clearly visible twisting corkscrew inversion, a single deliberate dramatic section, not a jumble of disconnected loops; 6) a high heavily banked outer horseshoe returning over a LOWER S-bend; 7) a more elaborate spiral around a compact power-house and a framed light tunnel returning toward a separate straight brake run and covered station. Give the viewer a legible alternating high/middle/near-ground ride rhythm with crossings at different heights. This must not remain a flat oval, not just the previous coaster scaled up, and not a giant tangle of anonymous rails. Use purposeful tower, tunnel and equipment volumes to frame the track and create near-miss sightlines while keeping visible clearance. A walkable observation path and access bridges weave BELOW or beside track, never through it; planted coastal edges connect to existing island road, no rectangular floating platform. Concentrate readable detail near station/tower/tunnel, low-poly functional small details at joints; no microscopic clutter. A tiny identical white helmet navy explorer and one orange/navy train establish scale. Clear warm-neutral daytime with readable shadows, normal perspective wide 3/4 elevated camera from southern entrance at about 20 m height, all heights visibly differentiated. Avoid fisheye, city skyline, rain, heavy fog, mirror materials, weapon themes, excessive text, labels, collage or UI. Keep believable modular game geometry. This is an aspirational spatial and ride-rhythm reference; no claim that a generated rail drawing is already validated engineering.

Use case: lighting-weather. Create the MATCHED NIGHT LIGHTING reference for the supplied expanded coastal cyberpunk roller-coaster concept. Change ONLY time of day and lighting, preserve exact expanded framing, scale, positions, track topology including steep drop, hills, inversion, spiral, low bends, all supports and buildings, same faceted coastal browser-game art, same explorers and train placements. Deep midnight cobalt sky and calm visible coast; no new city, haze, rain or mirror floors. Make the machinery, platform, ground and visitors clearly readable at normal screen brightness. Blue indirect moon/sky fill reveals the large tower faces, steel supports, train bodies and rocks, so the night image has three-dimensional volumes, never only bright lines on black. Cyan/teal technical lighting on selected track channels, tower ribs and tunnel; isolated restrained coral-magenta accents at inversion entry and gate controls. Warm amber light from station ceilings, inspection walkways, kiosk surfaces and low plaza lamps illuminates broad real surrounding surfaces with gentle contact shadows. Entrance, six lock modules, chest and all three puzzle bays remain identifiable. Stronger lighting hierarchy at station and entry; lower brightness on secondary machinery; retain dark recesses without losing walkable paths. Track high/mid/low layering must remain obvious. Polished stylized matte materials, mild tightly bounded glow, no blown-out bloom, no pure-black silhouettes, no cinematic depth-of-field hiding scenery. Full original landscape composition; no overlay text or comparison labels. This is a reference target for baked/vertex indirect lighting plus a small number of local lights, not unlimited per-lamp realtime illumination.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original production-minded visual calibration reference for a LARGE playable industrial INVENTORY INSPECTION YARD on a coastal island in a stylized third-person browser game. Two attached images are style references only: image 1 is actual game screenshot, keep its faceted environment and small white-helmet navy explorer proportions; image 2 is the approved-for-discussion rendering fidelity of a neighboring concept, use matching bevel scale and restrained material detail, but DO NOT copy its roller coaster, sci-fi equipment, neon, tower, layout or tracks. New scene: approximately 55 by 45 m industrial compound with three distinctly shaped functional sheds around a shared open working courtyard. Western tall open steel-coil bay: large hollow rolled-metal coils with layered cut edges and lifting cradles; visible gantry crane carrying a coil to expose a second coil; integrated ramp reaching an upper inspection gallery, actual returning stairs/paths, rails and mechanically supported beams. Northern medium shed: five kinds of storage containers, open shallow divided trays of hardware, weighing platform and inspection bench with naturally visible sample pieces. Eastern long logistics warehouse: a loading dock and truck with opened cargo bay, two pallets placed on a continuous roller route from storage to truck, dispatch barrier with a clearly lit amber status lamp. Give each bay its own readable silhouette, vertical hierarchy and useful work surfaces. A clear main pedestrian loop, protected crosswalk, secondary raised observation route, alcoves and convincing circulation around cargo. Function before clutter: riveted beam joints, limited ventilation louvers, rolled metal edges, load straps, hose reels, worn yellow floor markings, an electrical box, hanging work lamps, roof clerestories. Three small white-helmet navy game characters to establish scale; one operates crane, one inspects open pack. Restrained believable industrial palette: oxidized sage and blue-gray corrugated roofs, warm concrete, dull cool steel coil bodies, mustard crane, dark timber pallets, sparse coastal grass/flowers in planting beds and faceted rocks at shore edges. Wide 3/4 slightly elevated camera from south entrance, enough view into all three bays and both routes. Daytime under neutral afternoon sun, shaded interiors readable through skylights and soft reflected light. Polished medium-detail low-poly game-art style matching existing island, not photoreal or toy block boxes, no giant HUD/callouts/chart panels, no brand logos or false real-company industrial imagery, no weapons, no pollution story, no generic cyberpunk overlay. This is a fictional playable interpretation of IBD inventory fieldwork, not an actual company's factory. Landscape composition; single cohesive scene, no collage or annotation. Make physical inspection, moving cargo and alternate viewpoints the visual story.
